description:
FILED s474b (Fable, 2026-09-07) while answering the USER's question "what is the mechanism behind op/numconvert.t".  The row-shortfall row `t/op/numconvert.t 1446 UNEXPLAINED` now carries this cause.

MECHANISM (one, with three faces): perl's scalars carry IV (signed 64), UV (unsigned 64) and NV (double); integer arithmetic that leaves the 64-bit range PROMOTES TO NV, `use integer` does C signed wraparound, and sprintf %u/%d clamp or reinterpret at the boundary.  PCL's numbers are SBCL integers (unbounded) plus double-floats, so there is no boundary anywhere: 9 of 12 probe lines diverge (scratch numconv.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
  ~0 ** 6                       perl 3.94020061963945e+115     PCL the exact 116-digit integer
  sprintf "%u", ~0 ** 6         perl 18446744073709551615      PCL the 116-digit integer (no clamp)
  use integer; ~0 * 16          perl -16                       PCL 295147905179352825840
  ~0 * 16                       perl 2.95147905179353e+20      PCL 295147905179352825840
  ~0 + 1                        perl 1.84467440737096e+19      PCL 18446744073709551616
  use integer; IV_MAX + 1       perl -9223372036854775808      PCL 9223372036854775808
  sprintf "%d", ~0              perl -1                        PCL 18446744073709551615
  2**64                         perl 1.84467440737096e+19      PCL 18446744073709551616
  use integer; 2**63            perl 9.22337203685478e+18      PCL 9223372036854775808
  (agree: IV_MAX+1 outside `use integer` = 9223372036854775808 both; -3 % 5 = 2 / -3 both; ~0-3 != ~0 both)

WHY numconvert.t is ALL-OR-NOTHING: its preamble computes `$max_uv2 = sprintf "%u", ~0 ** 6` and `$big_iv = do { use integer; ~0 * 16 }` and prints `1..0 # Skip unsigned perl arithmetic is not sane` unless max_uv2 eq ~0 and big_iv <= ~0.  Both are bignums in PCL, so the file never plans its 1446 rows.  Those rows then test every conversion chain among U/I/N/P representations (converters *2..*9 in the file header) -- with one integer type PCL would fail a large share of them even after the preamble passes; the preamble is the cheap discriminating measurement, the rows are the real bar.

WHAT IT WOULD TAKE (a design, Fable; perf-sensitive -- Target A): (1) integer results outside [-2^63, 2^64) promote to double at the operator (SBCL fixnum ops already branch to bignum there; the branch becomes a float conversion -- the fast path is untouched); (2) `use integer` regions wrap to signed 64 (`(logand ...)`/`sb-c::mask-signed-field`) -- today the region emits bare CL ops (#1175/#1000); (3) sprintf %u/%d/%x clamp/reinterpret at the boundary; (4) the internal callers that NEED exact 2**N (cl/pack-impl.pl lines 297/1187, lib/Math/BigInt/Calc.pm) get an explicit integer-power helper (memory project_power_op_float_divergence already lists them).  Related: not-supported.md "`**` returns an exact integer where Perl returns a float (NV)" (USER-parked 2026-06-26), "`use integer` - large shift / overflow edge cases" (bop.t 481/482), #1000, #1175.  Row count behind it: numconvert.t 1446 (companion) + bop.t 2 (sweep) + whatever the #1501 census attributes.  NOT to be started without the USER: it changes a number representation decision the USER parked.


=== RE-SCOPED (s474b, Fable, 2026-09-07) -- USER: "Sounds good" to DOCUMENTING rather than implementing the boundary ===
Evidence that made it the right call: 22 modules use `use integer` across perl's core lib + the on-disk CPAN dists (B::Deparse, Locale::Maketext, Math::BigInt::Calc, Pod::Simple x3, Tie::SubstrHash, Unicode::UCD, Digest::SHA, Time::Piece, Algorithm::Diff x2, URI::_punycode, ...) and NONE relies on wraparound -- truncating division and speed only; Tie::SubstrHash bounds its own hash accumulator at 1e13 every iteration (perl's boundary is platform-dependent, so authors never could rely on it); pure-Perl digests mask with 0xffffffff explicitly, which works on unbounded integers.

THE JOB (a small Opus filler, after #1061):
 1. ONE `docs/not-supported.md` entry "Integers are unbounded: no 64-bit boundary" that absorbs the existing `**`-returns-an-exact-integer and `use integer`-large-shift entries (leave a one-line pointer at each old heading; grep Pl/t and the baselines for the old section TITLES -- rows cite them by name, and every citation is re-pointed in the same commit).  It states plainly: integer arithmetic never overflows to a float (`~0 + 1`, `2**64` print exact); `use integer` never wraps (`~0 * 16` is exact, not -16); `sprintf "%d", ~0` prints the unsigned value, `%u` above UV_MAX prints in full; code that masks explicitly behaves as in perl, code relying on implicit wrap gets the exact value SILENTLY; and the HAZARD: an unmasked accumulator loop grows without bound (quadratic time + memory) where perl wraps or goes float.  Point at #1513 as the revisit pointer and name the trigger.
 2. `baselines/perl-suite-expected.tsv`: register `op/numconvert.t` citing the section (the file skips ITSELF on its preamble); re-run it alone (`tools/run-perl-suite.pl --jobs 1 op/numconvert.t`) and splice the XDIFF verdict into `baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv` by hand; `baselines/row-shortfall.tsv` row already carries the cause (s474b) -- update it to cite the section.
 3. `docs/DECIDED.md` one-line pointer; `docs/ir-spec.md` numeric model paragraph says it normatively (integers = CL integers; doubles; no IV/UV distinction).
 4. Guard: a `Pl/t` row asserting the documented behaviour (the 9 divergent probe lines above ARE the fixture: assert PCL's answers, so a future boundary implementation trips it deliberately).
No emission change; corpus-diff IDENTICAL; the companion leg is the one file.

SEE ALSO the USER's follow-up question (s474b): whether `my` variables inside `use integer` should be DECLARED integer for speed -- answered in DECIDED Â§s474b; the measurement is there.


=== DONE (s473a, 2026-09-07, commit 20dd6a78) ===
All four items delivered; no emission change (corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111).

 1. docs/not-supported.md gained "Integers are unbounded: PCL has no 64-bit
    boundary".  It ABSORBS the `**`-returns-an-exact-integer and `use integer`
    -large-shift entries, both headings kept as pointers because rows cite them
    BY NAME; the three citations were re-pointed in the same commit â
    baselines/fail-baseline.tsv rows 110/111 (bop.t 481/482) and
    docs/difftest-fuzzer.md:50.  Contents: the three faces (no overflow-to-NV,
    no `use integer` wrap, no %u/%d clamp); the nine divergence rows as a
    table; the neighbours that AGREE (IV_MAX+1 outside `use integer`, -3 % 5
    both ways, ~0 itself), which is what makes the divergence narrow; the
    explicit-mask rule; the unbounded-accumulator HAZARD; the revisit trigger.
 2. baselines/perl-suite-expected.tsv registers op/numconvert.t; --bless-rows
    added the one diverging row (*summary*); DIFF -> XDIFF with counts
    UNCHANGED (1446/0 vs 0/0), `--jobs 1`, the #366 serial re-run agreeing,
    spliced into baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv by hand with a header note.
    baselines/row-shortfall.tsv's row now cites the section.
 3. docs/DECIDED.md Â§s473a; docs/ir-spec.md Â§2.6 gained a normative
    "The numeric model" paragraph.
 4. Guard Pl/t/int-boundary-01.t, 19 rows, 0.43 s.  It asserts CURRENT
    behaviour ON PURPOSE and says so; inverse verification is N/A.  Row 1 pins
    the section HEADING, because three baselines and one doc cite it by name.

TWO CORRECTIONS to the probe lines this task was filed with, both precedence:
`~0 ** 6` is `~(0**6)` = `~0`, and `use integer; ~0 * 16` is -16 on BOTH sides
(PCL's `~` under the pragma is already perl's).  The real divergences need the
value in a VARIABLE first, which is how t/op/numconvert.t's own preamble
writes them ($max_uv1 ** 6, do { use integer; $max_uv1 * 16 }); the shipped
table uses that spelling.

ONE FINDING the task did not have â THE EXPLICIT-MASK RULE HAS A LIMIT, found
by probing the rule rather than restating it.  Masking every step is
byte-identical to perl (the pure-Perl digest idiom, 3685539155 over the
pangram), but a mask applied AFTER an already-overflowed intermediate
diverges: `0xffffffff & (~0 * 16)` is 4294967295 in perl, because its NV
CLAMPS to UV_MAX on the way into `&`, and 4294967280 in PCL.  Both rows are in
the section and in the guard.
subject: DOCUMENT (USER 2026-09-07 "Sounds good"): PCL has NO 64-bit integer boundary, by design -- ONE not-supported entry (folds the `**`-returns-exact and `use integer`-shift entries; states overflow-to-NV / `use integer` wrap / %u %d clamp are absent, the explicit-mask rule, the unbounded-accumulator hazard); register t/op/numconvert.t as an EXPECTED divergence (its 1446 rows leave UNEXPLAINED); revisit trigger = a CPAN module failing its own tests by relying on wrap
